newsitem.title: PANAMA: Colombian drug lord stashed riches in Panama-police.
newsitem.headline: Colombian drug lord stashed riches in Panama-police.

text.p: An accused Colombian drug lord linked to a political scandal in Panama allegedly stashed millions of dollars in a local bank which is under investigation for money laundering, a Panama police source said on Monday.

Jose Castrillon Henao, who allegedly controlled the Cali cartel's seagoing operations, has been in a Panama City prison since April and police drug units are investigating a complex network of bank accounts that he operated.

Castrillon, whose net worth is estimated at $50 million, donated $51,000 to the 1994 presidential campaign of President Ernesto Perez Balladares, said a police source involved in the investigation who asked not to be identified. Government officials were recently cleared of any wrongdoing.

"We're investigating an apparent network of accounts operated by Castrillon of at least $20 to $30 million in Banaico (Banco Agroindustrial y Comercial)," the source said, adding that millions more were stashed in other banks.
"Castrillon's network had several accounts in several banks in Panama ... but this doesn't mean the banks have committed crimes," the source said.
Banaico was ordered shut earlier this year for liquidity problems and remains under investigation for money laundering. No one has been arrested in the Banaico case.

Mexican anti-drug officials are expected to arrive on Monday or Tuesday to investigate alleged ties between Castrillon and Manuel Rodriguez Lopez, one of Mexico's leading drug traffickers, the source said.
